newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares shed further gains on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares shed further gains on profit-taking.

text.p: Jordanian stocks fell on Tuesday for a second day, with profit-taking and year-end portfolio selling weighing on prices, dealers said.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.39 percent to 153.88 points in this year's highest turnover worth 3.2 million dinars ($4.5 million).
High volume was dominated by large bloc sales in market heavyweights Arab Bank, Arab Potash and Jordan Phosphate Mines in year-end portfolio settlements, brokers said.
Profit-taking was focused on industrials that had been steadily rising since news last month of Iraq's imminent implementation of its oil-for food deal.

The market, buoyed by Iraq prospects, soared on Saturday to its highest level in 11 months that has reversed months of decline over a tight monetary policy diverting funds from the bourse and political uncertainty over Middle East peace.
Brokers said investor sentiment continues to be buttressed by optimism Jordan will stand to gain from Iraq's oil-for-food deal with traders and industrialists clinching some of its lucrative deals.

Some detergent and vegetable oil firms that stand to benefit from Iraq's "oil-for-food" deals were among the top gainers, with Industrial Commercial Agricultural rising close to a maximum 5 percent to 2.59 dinars. Arab Chemical Detergent rose 2.94 percent to 8.75 dinars.
Overall losers outstripped gainers, with 39 stocks falling while only 6 gained. Another seven traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of 45 best-traded shares fell 1 percent to 82.65, still 13.47 percent down on last year.
